subject: Day 0: confirm hospital screens; pediatrician visit by day 3-5
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 0. Survival and stabilization. Weight loss of 5-10% from birth weight is expected this week; the floor for concern is 7%. Output, feeds, and color trajectory dominate the agenda for the first seven days.

Action items
- Call your chosen pediatrician within 24 hours of hospital discharge and schedule Avi's first-week visit for day 3-5. The hospital pediatrician will instruct you to do this; do it before discharge paperwork distracts you. (https://www.healthychildren.org/English/family-life/health-management/Pages/default.aspx)
- Confirm two state-mandated screens passed before discharge: the metabolic newborn screen and the CCHD pulse-oximetry screen. PKU, MCADD, and congenital hypothyroidism have narrow treatment windows. CDC overview: https://www.cdc.gov/newborn-screening/about/index.html
- File birth certificate paperwork before discharge if the hospital offers it. Avi's Social Security number follows by mail in 2-4 weeks; you will need it for the 529 plan and the dependent tax claim. SSA application page: https://www.ssa.gov/ssnumber/
- Set up the pediatrician's online portal for messaging and after-hours triage. Save the practice's after-hours triage line to phone favorites.
- Lactation consultant on speed dial. The first 72 hours post-discharge is the highest-failure-rate window for establishing breastfeeding. International Lactation Consultant Association: https://ilca.org/

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Newborn rash (erythema toxicum), peeling skin, milia, occasional sneezes or hiccups, a single black-tarry meconium stool stuck in the diaper.
- [low concern] Weight loss up to 7% of birth weight, regained by day 10-14.
- [monitor] Weight loss 7-10%; the pediatrician will assess feeding effectiveness at the first-week visit.
- [call within 24h] Yellow tinge spreading from face to chest and belly (jaundice descending caudally; bilirubin is climbing). Fewer than 6 wet diapers by day 5. Persistent inability to latch. Weight loss greater than 10%. AAP HealthyChildren on jaundice: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Jaundice.aspx
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C). In infants under 90 days this is a workup-required event, full stop. Lethargy, refusing all feeds, blue or grey color, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting with each breath, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. If any persist or worsen, call 911!

Enrichment opportunity
Skin-to-skin as the default holding mode for the next two weeks. It regulates his temperature, glucose, and breathing, and supports milk supply if breastfeeding. CDC on breastfeeding and skin-to-skin: https://www.cdc.gov/breastfeeding/index.html

Upcoming
- Day 3-5: first-week pediatrician visit (target window).
- Day 7-10: weight check; most term infants regain birth weight by day 14.
- Day 28-35: 1-month well visit window opens.

Further reading
- Bringing Up Bébé by Pamela Druckerman — French-American framing for the first months: https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/books/207651/bringing-up-bebe-by-pamela-druckerman/
- Cribsheet by Emily Oster — evidence-driven decisions from birth to preschool: https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/books/562146/cribsheet-by-emily-oster/
- AAP HealthyChildren overview of the first month: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/default.aspx
- CDC newborn screening explainer for parents: https://www.cdc.gov/newborn-screening/about/index.html
